An internet service provider connects homes, schools and businesses to the internet over cable, fiber, mobile or satellite links.
One of the first commercial dial-up internet providers, The World, opened to the public in the United States in 1989.
More than 5 billion people, about two thirds of humanity, now use the internet (International Telecommunication Union).
An e-government portal puts public services such as applications, certificates and payments in one online place, so citizens do not have to visit offices.
Estonia's X-Road system, launched in 2001, lets government databases exchange data securely, so citizens rarely have to give the state the same information twice.
Azerbaijan's ASAN Xidmət centers, opened in 2012, bring services from many agencies under one roof, and the model has received a United Nations Public Service Award.
Which country built the X-Road data exchange system?
Mobile banking lets people pay, save and transfer money with a phone, even where there are few bank branches.
M-Pesa, launched in Kenya in 2007, let people send money by text message and became one of the world's best-known mobile money services.
Mobile money helped hundreds of millions of adults in developing countries open their first financial account (World Bank Global Findex).
Which mobile money service launched in Kenya in 2007?
A fiber backbone carries huge amounts of data between cities and countries as pulses of light inside thin glass fibers.
Undersea fiber-optic cables carry the vast majority of data traveling between continents; satellites carry only a small share.
Light in an optical fiber travels at about two thirds of its speed in a vacuum, roughly 200,000 km per second.
What carries the data inside an optical fiber?
Fintech companies use software to offer financial services such as payments, lending and investing faster and more cheaply.
In 2016 the UK's Financial Conduct Authority opened one of the first regulatory sandboxes, where fintech startups test products with real customers under supervision.
Many countries have copied the sandbox idea, so regulators can learn about new technology before writing rules.
A supervised space to test new financial products
Data centers are buildings full of servers that store data and run the apps and websites people use every day.
The International Energy Agency estimates that data centers use roughly 1 to 1.5 percent of the world's electricity.
Cooling is one of the biggest costs of a data center, so many are built in cold climates such as the Nordic countries.
Besides electricity, what do data centers need most to keep servers running?
A digital ID lets people prove who they are online, sign documents and use services securely with a card, phone or code.
India's Aadhaar program gives residents a 12-digit identity number linked to fingerprints and iris scans, and more than a billion people are enrolled.
Estonia's chip-based ID card, introduced in 2002, lets citizens sign documents digitally with the same legal weight as a handwritten signature.
How many digits does an Aadhaar number have?
5G is the fifth generation of mobile networks. It offers higher speeds, lower delay and room for far more connected devices than 4G.
South Korea launched the world's first nationwide commercial 5G service in April 2019.
Low delay (latency) matters for things like remote surgery, factory robots and self-driving cars.
What does the "G" in 5G stand for?
An open data portal publishes government data, such as transport, weather or budgets, for anyone to use for free.
The United States launched data.gov in 2009 and the United Kingdom launched data.gov.uk in 2010.
Developers use open transport data to build route-planning apps, often faster than governments could build them.
Data anyone can freely use and share
A cloud platform rents computing power and storage over the internet, so organizations do not need to run their own servers.
Amazon Web Services launched its first public cloud services, S3 storage and EC2 computing, in 2006.
Many governments follow a "cloud first" policy: they consider cloud services before buying their own hardware.
What does "the cloud" mean in computing?
Computing resources delivered over the internet
Instant payment systems move money between bank accounts in seconds, at any time of day, often by scanning a QR code.
India's UPI, launched in 2016, now handles billions of payments every month, and Brazil's Pix, launched in 2020, was adopted by most Brazilian adults within a few years.
Instant payments can lower costs for small shops, because their fees are usually much lower than card fees.
What is the name of Brazil's instant payment system?
E-health services let doctors and patients share records, book visits and get prescriptions online.
Estonia introduced nationwide digital prescriptions in 2010; patients collect their medicine at a pharmacy just by showing an ID.
Shared health records help doctors avoid repeating tests and spot dangerous drug combinations.
The Internet of Things connects everyday objects, such as meters, lights and sensors, so they can send data and be controlled remotely.
The term "Internet of Things" was coined by Kevin Ashton in 1999.
Smart water meters can detect leaks automatically, saving water and money.
A smart city uses sensors and data to run traffic, energy, water and public services more efficiently.
Singapore launched its Smart Nation initiative in 2014 to use digital technology across government and daily life.
Adaptive traffic lights that react to real-time traffic can shorten journeys without building new roads.
Which country launched the "Smart Nation" initiative in 2014?
E-education brings lessons, textbooks and exams online, so students can learn anywhere.
Coursera and edX, two of the best-known platforms for massive open online courses, were both founded in 2012.
When schools closed during COVID-19 in 2020, more than 1.5 billion students worldwide were affected, pushing schools online almost overnight (UNESCO).
An AI lab builds systems that learn from data to recognize images, understand language and make predictions.
The term "artificial intelligence" was coined for a 1956 workshop at Dartmouth College organized by John McCarthy and others.
Many countries now publish national AI strategies; Canada released one of the first in 2017.
When was the term "artificial intelligence" coined for the Dartmouth workshop?
Robots are machines that sense their surroundings and carry out physical tasks, from welding cars to delivering parcels.
The word "robot" comes from Karel Čapek's 1920 play R.U.R.; it is based on the Czech word "robota", meaning forced labor.
South Korea has one of the highest numbers of industrial robots per factory worker in the world (International Federation of Robotics).
Where does the word "robot" come from?
Autonomous transport uses sensors and AI so cars, buses and trucks can drive with little or no human help.
Engineers use the SAE scale of driving automation, which runs from Level 0 (no automation) to Level 5 (full automation).
Driverless robotaxi services already carry paying passengers in some cities, such as Phoenix and San Francisco in the United States.
How many levels does the SAE driving automation scale have?
A semiconductor fab is a factory that makes computer chips by printing billions of tiny transistors onto silicon wafers.
In 1965 Gordon Moore predicted that the number of transistors on a chip would keep doubling at a steady pace; this became known as Moore's law.
Taiwan's TSMC is the world's largest contract chipmaker, producing chips designed by many other companies.
The number of transistors on a chip
Quantum computers use qubits, which can be in a mix of 0 and 1 at the same time, to solve certain problems much faster than ordinary computers.
In 2019 Google reported that its 53-qubit Sycamore processor finished a specific calculation far faster than classical supercomputers could.
Many quantum computers must be kept close to absolute zero, colder than outer space, to keep their qubits stable.
What is the basic unit of information in a quantum computer?
Biotechnology uses living cells and DNA to develop medicines, vaccines, crops and new materials.
Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing CRISPR gene editing.
mRNA vaccine technology allowed the first COVID-19 vaccines to be developed and approved in less than a year.
Satellite internet beams connectivity from orbit, reaching ships, planes and remote villages that cables cannot reach.
Geostationary satellites orbit about 35,800 km above the equator, while low Earth orbit constellations fly only a few hundred to about 2,000 km up, which cuts delay.
Azerbaijan launched its first telecommunications satellite, Azerspace-1, in 2013.
Why do low Earth orbit satellites have lower delay than geostationary ones?
They are much closer to Earth
Fusion power aims to produce energy the way the Sun does, by joining light atoms together, without carbon emissions.
In December 2022 the US National Ignition Facility became the first experiment to get more energy out of a fusion reaction than the laser energy put in.
ITER, a fusion reactor being built in southern France by the EU, China, India, Japan, South Korea, Russia and the US, is one of the largest science projects in the world.
What natural object is powered by nuclear fusion?
A space agency builds and launches satellites and spacecraft for communication, Earth observation, navigation and science.
The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, in 1957.
Earth observation satellites help countries track crops, floods, wildfires and climate change.
What was the first artificial satellite?
Online tax systems let people and companies file and pay taxes in minutes, often with forms the state has already filled in.
In Estonia most people file their income tax return online, and returns are pre-filled with data the tax office already has.
Pre-filled returns reduce mistakes and save huge amounts of paperwork every year.
What is a pre-filled tax return?
A return the tax office fills in with data it already has
A tax paid years in advance
A paper form sent by mail
E-commerce means buying and selling goods and services online.
Amazon started in 1995 as an online bookstore, and Alibaba was founded in China in 1999.
Online shops let small businesses sell to customers in other countries without opening stores there.
A central bank digital currency (CBDC) is a digital form of a country's money, issued by its central bank.
The Bahamas launched the Sand Dollar in 2020, one of the first CBDCs in the world.
A CBDC differs from cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin because a central bank issues and backs it.
Smart contracts are programs stored on a blockchain that carry out an agreement automatically when conditions are met.
Computer scientist Nick Szabo described the idea in the 1990s, and the Ethereum blockchain, launched in 2015, made smart contracts widely used.
Because the code runs automatically, a bug in a smart contract can be very costly, so independent code audits are common.
Where do smart contracts usually run?
Open banking lets customers safely share their bank data with other apps through secure interfaces called APIs.
The United Kingdom required its largest banks to support open banking in 2018, alongside the EU's PSD2 payment rules.
Open banking powers budgeting apps that show all of a person's bank accounts in one place.
Tokenization records ownership of assets such as bonds, property or art as digital tokens that can be traded and divided easily.
Several governments and banks have tested issuing bonds as digital tokens on blockchain platforms.
Dividing an asset into tokens can let many small investors each own a share of something expensive.
Represents an asset as digital tokens
In a real-time economy, invoices, payments and tax reports flow automatically between computer systems instead of on paper.
Italy made electronic invoicing mandatory for most business-to-business sales in 2019.
E-invoicing helps tax offices detect fraud faster, because the data arrives as transactions happen.
What replaces paper invoices in a real-time economy?
Electronic health records store a patient's history, test results and prescriptions digitally, so doctors can see them when needed.
In Estonia, patients can log in to see their own health records and check which doctors have viewed them.
Shared records mean a patient does not have to repeat their full medical history at every new clinic.
Why are shared electronic health records useful?
Doctors can see a patient's history quickly
Online learning uses video lessons, interactive exercises and virtual classrooms to teach people anywhere.
Khan Academy, founded in 2008, offers free lessons used by millions of students around the world.
Short practice quizzes, like this one, help people remember what they learn. Scientists call this the testing effect.
Electronic signatures let people sign contracts and forms online with legal force.
The EU's eIDAS regulation of 2014 says a qualified electronic signature has the same legal effect as a handwritten one.
Digital signatures use cryptography, so any change to a signed document can be detected.
Under EU eIDAS rules, a qualified e-signature has the same effect as what?
Universal connectivity means every person, including people in rural areas, can get affordable internet access.
In 2010 Finland became one of the first countries to make broadband internet access a legal right.
The gap between people with and without internet access is called the digital divide.
The gap between people with and without internet access
Internet voting lets citizens cast their vote securely online using a digital ID.
Estonia became the first country to allow online voting in nationwide elections, starting with local elections in 2005.
In Estonia, online voters can change their vote during the voting period, which helps protect them from being pressured.
Which country first allowed online voting in nationwide elections?
Telemedicine lets patients see doctors by video or chat and share data from devices at home.
Telemedicine use grew sharply during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, when many clinics moved appointments online.
Telemedicine helps people in remote areas reach specialists without traveling long distances.
Digital literacy is the ability to use digital tools safely and well, from writing emails to spotting fake news and scams.
Finland teaches students to recognize misinformation as part of its school curriculum and regularly tops European media literacy rankings.
Many successful cyber attacks start with a person being tricked, for example by a phishing email.
Tricking people into giving away information
A firewall checks network traffic and blocks connections that break security rules.
Network firewalls became common in the late 1980s and early 1990s, as companies connected their networks to the internet.
Firewalls are named after the fire walls in buildings that stop a fire from spreading.
Threat intelligence is information about attackers, their tools and methods, shared so defenders can prepare.
MITRE ATT&CK, a free public knowledge base of attacker techniques released in 2015, is used by security teams around the world.
Many countries run a national CERT (computer emergency response team) that warns organizations about new threats.
What is the main purpose of threat intelligence?
Learning how attackers work, to prepare defenses
Public key infrastructure (PKI) uses key pairs and digital certificates so computers can prove who they are and encrypt data.
When you see the padlock in a browser's address bar, the website is using a PKI certificate to set up an encrypted HTTPS connection.
In a key pair, the public key can be shared with anyone, while the private key must stay secret.
Which key in a key pair can be shared with anyone?
Zero trust security assumes that no user or device is trusted by default, even inside the network; every request must be verified.
In 2021 the US government directed federal agencies to move toward zero trust security architectures.
The motto of zero trust is "never trust, always verify".
What is the motto of zero trust security?
AI threat detection uses machine learning to spot unusual activity, such as strange logins or traffic, faster than people can.
Security teams receive so many alerts every day that AI tools are used to separate real attacks from false alarms.
Attackers use AI too, for example to write more convincing phishing messages.
What does AI threat detection look for?
Unusual activity that may be an attack
Post-quantum cryptography is encryption designed to stay secure even against future quantum computers.
In August 2024 the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) published its first post-quantum encryption standards.
Attackers may "harvest now, decrypt later": steal encrypted data today and decrypt it once quantum computers are powerful enough.
Why do we need post-quantum cryptography?
Future quantum computers could break today's encryption
Cyber resilience is the ability to keep running and recover quickly after an attack, using backups, drills and response plans.
The widely used 3-2-1 backup rule says: keep three copies of your data, on two kinds of storage, with one copy offsite.
Ransomware locks data until a ransom is paid; good offline backups let organizations recover without paying.
In the 3-2-1 backup rule, how many copies should be kept offsite?
TCP/IP is the set of rules that lets different computers and networks talk to each other. It is the foundation of the internet.
On 1 January 1983 the ARPANET switched to TCP/IP, a date often called the birthday of the internet.
TCP/IP was designed by Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn in the 1970s.
The basic communication rules of the internet
IPv6 is the newer version of the internet's addressing system, created because the older IPv4 was running out of addresses.
IPv4 has about 4.3 billion addresses, while IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses, about 3.4 × 10³⁸ of them.
IPv6 was standardized in the late 1990s, and today a large share of internet traffic, especially on mobile networks, uses it.
IPv4 was running out of addresses
Virtualization lets one physical server run many separate virtual machines, using hardware far more efficiently.
Virtualization makes cloud computing possible: cloud providers rent out virtual machines instead of whole physical servers.
IBM ran virtual machines on its mainframe computers as early as the 1960s and 1970s.
What does virtualization let one server do?
An internet exchange point (IXP) is a place where networks connect directly to swap traffic locally.
Countries with local IXPs keep domestic traffic inside the country instead of routing it abroad, which makes it faster and cheaper.
The largest IXPs, such as those in Frankfurt and Amsterdam, handle traffic of many terabits per second.
What is an internet exchange point?
A place where networks connect to swap traffic
Edge computing processes data close to where it is created, such as in a factory or a cell tower, instead of in a faraway data center.
Self-driving cars and factory robots rely on edge computing because they must react within milliseconds.
Processing data locally can also protect privacy, because less personal data has to leave the device.
To process data close to where it is created
A smart grid uses sensors and software to balance electricity supply and demand in real time.
Smart electricity meters, now installed in millions of European homes, let utilities and customers track and reduce consumption.
Smart grids make it easier to use solar and wind power, whose output changes with the weather.
What does a smart grid balance?
A digital twin is a virtual copy of a real object or system, such as a building, factory or city, kept up to date with live data.
Singapore built "Virtual Singapore", a detailed 3D model of the city, to help plan and test projects.
Engineers can test changes on a digital twin first, so mistakes cost nothing in the real world.
A virtual copy of a real system
Machine learning lets computers learn patterns from examples instead of following only hand-written rules.
Arthur Samuel popularized the term "machine learning" in 1959 while building a program that learned to play checkers.
Email spam filters were one of the first machine learning tools used by millions of people every day.
Big data means datasets so large and fast-moving that they need special tools to store and analyze.
Big data is often described with the "three Vs": volume, velocity and variety.
Cities analyze anonymized transport data to plan bus routes and reduce traffic jams.
What are the "three Vs" of big data?
Deep learning uses artificial neural networks with many layers to learn complex patterns in images, sound and text.
In 2012 a deep learning model called AlexNet won the ImageNet image-recognition competition by a wide margin, starting the modern AI boom.
Artificial neural networks are loosely inspired by how neurons in the brain connect.
Transformers are a neural network design that processes whole sequences at once using "attention". They power today's large language models.
Researchers at Google introduced the transformer in 2017 in a paper titled "Attention Is All You Need".
The "T" in GPT stands for transformer: Generative Pre-trained Transformer.
What does the "T" in GPT stand for?
Quantum algorithms are step-by-step methods designed to run on quantum computers and take advantage of qubits.
In 1994 Peter Shor showed that a large quantum computer could factor big numbers quickly, which would break widely used RSA encryption.
Grover's algorithm, from 1996, can search an unsorted list much faster than any classical method.
Neuromorphic chips are processors designed to work like networks of brain neurons, using very little power.
IBM's TrueNorth chip, presented in 2014, had about one million artificial neurons.
The human brain runs on roughly 20 watts, about as much as a dim light bulb, which is why engineers study it to build efficient chips.
What are neuromorphic chips inspired by?
AI alignment is research on making AI systems pursue the goals people intend, safely and honestly.
The United Kingdom and the United States both set up AI safety institutes in 2023 to test advanced AI models.
AI can find unexpected shortcuts to reach a goal, so goals have to be specified very carefully.
Making AI pursue intended goals safely
Efficient data centers cut the energy used for cooling and power conversion, so more of it goes to computing.
Efficiency is measured with PUE (power usage effectiveness). A perfect score is 1.0, and the most efficient large data centers reach about 1.1.
Some data centers reuse their waste heat to warm nearby homes, for example in Finland and Denmark.
What does a PUE of 1.0 mean?
All energy goes to the computing equipment
The data center is switched off
It runs only on solar power
Renewable power comes from sources that are naturally replenished, such as sunlight, wind, flowing water and geothermal heat.
Iceland produces almost all of its electricity from hydropower and geothermal energy.
Solar panel prices fell by around 90 percent during the 2010s, making solar one of the cheapest sources of new electricity.
Which of these is a renewable energy source?
E-waste recycling recovers valuable materials such as copper, gold and rare metals from old electronics.
The Global E-waste Monitor found the world produced about 62 million tonnes of e-waste in 2022, and less than a quarter was properly collected and recycled.
A tonne of old phones contains much more gold than a tonne of typical gold ore.
To recover valuable materials and reduce pollution
Because electronics are made of paper
Smart mobility combines public transport, bike sharing, ride sharing and apps to move people efficiently with less pollution.
Tallinn, Estonia's capital, has offered free public transport to its registered residents since 2013.
Mobility-as-a-service apps let travelers plan and pay for buses, trains and scooters in one place.
What is a goal of smart mobility?
Moving people efficiently with less pollution
Carbon accounting measures how much greenhouse gas an organization or country emits, so it can plan reductions.
The Greenhouse Gas Protocol sorts emissions into Scope 1 (direct), Scope 2 (from purchased energy) and Scope 3 (across the supply chain).
For many companies, Scope 3 emissions from suppliers and customers are the largest part of their footprint.
Green hydrogen is made by splitting water with electricity from renewable sources, so producing it emits no carbon.
Hydrogen can replace fossil fuels in heavy industry, such as steelmaking, where batteries are hard to use.
Splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen with electricity is called electrolysis.
Energy storage, such as large batteries, saves electricity when it is plentiful and releases it when it is needed.
Lithium-ion battery prices fell by roughly 90 percent between 2010 and 2020, making grid-scale batteries affordable.
Pumped hydro, which pumps water uphill and lets it flow back down through turbines, is still the largest form of grid energy storage in the world.
What does grid energy storage do?
Saves electricity until it is needed
Government, bank and news websites are flooded with traffic and keep going offline.
In April and May 2007, Estonia was hit by weeks of cyber attacks on government, bank and media websites. In 2008, NATO opened its Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence in Tallinn.
Create a national cyber defense unit
Take services offline until it passes
A fast-spreading illness forces every school in the country to close for weeks.
When schools closed during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, more than 1.5 billion students worldwide were affected, and many countries moved lessons online almost overnight (UNESCO).
Wait for the situation to improve
Factories around the world cannot get enough computer chips, and prices are rising fast.
From 2020 to 2023, a global semiconductor shortage slowed the production of cars, consoles and electronics, and several governments funded new chip factories.
Hospital computers are locked, and the attackers demand a ransom to unlock them.

In May 2017, the WannaCry ransomware infected hundreds of thousands of computers worldwide and disrupted parts of the UK's National Health Service. Authorities usually advise victims not to pay, because payment funds criminals and does not guarantee recovery.
Restore from backups and patch every system
Run hospitals on paper for a while
A ship's anchor has damaged the main undersea internet cable to your country.

In 2008, damage to undersea cables in the Mediterranean Sea disrupted internet access for millions of people in the Middle East and South Asia. Most traffic between continents travels through such cables.
A popular app secretly sold its users' personal data, and citizens are angry.
The EU's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) took effect in May 2018. It gives people rights over their personal data and allows large fines for companies that misuse it.
Pass a strong data protection law
A strong geomagnetic storm is about to hit Earth and could damage satellites and power grids.

In February 2022, SpaceX lost dozens of newly launched Starlink satellites after a geomagnetic storm increased atmospheric drag. In 1859, the Carrington Event caused telegraph systems to fail around the world.
Put satellites and the grid in safe mode
Young engineers are moving abroad for better jobs.
In 2014, Estonia launched e-Residency, a digital identity that lets people anywhere in the world start and run an Estonian company online.
A national election is coming, and citizens ask to vote online.
Estonia was the first country to allow internet voting in nationwide elections, starting with local elections in 2005. Online voters can change their vote during the voting period.
Fake AI-made videos of national leaders are spreading on social media.
Ahead of elections in 2024, several countries saw AI-generated fake audio and video of politicians. Many governments responded with media literacy campaigns and rules for labelling AI-made content.
Record temperatures push electricity demand to its limit.
Heatwaves raise electricity demand for cooling. Smart grids can ask devices to use less power at peak times, which is called demand response.
A new instant payment app is spreading fast, and banks want it slowed down.
India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI), launched in 2016, grew to billions of payments a month within a few years and is now used by shops of every size.
Let it grow with light regulation
License it with strict security rules
Protect the banks and block it
